decisions.decision: Fixed 'stuck'/truncated whole-receipt IMAGE prints over the network by bypassing DantSu with our OWN paced GS v 0 band sender. Root cause: DantSu's DeviceConnection.send() has no drain (the RN fork ADDED one) — it sends the raster in one un-paced blob, and our D32 end-drain was too coarse for a big image; the RN package paces every send.
decisions.design: New escpos/EscPosRaster (pure control bytes INIT/align/feed/cut + bands(bitmap, bandHeight=128) -> list of GS v 0 commands, 1-bit MSB-first, dark = lum<384). EscPosNetworkPrinter.doPrint routes a SINGLE-Image document (PrintType.IMAGE always produces one) to new printImagePaced(): opens its own Socket (retry via retryPolicy, sendBufferSize=16KB), scales/dithers/inverts via Bitmaps, writes ESC @ + ESC a align, then each GS v 0 band with out.write+flush+delay((band.size/64).coerceIn(5,400)) — PER-BAND PACING so the printer keeps up, then ESC d feed + GS V cut. Text/columns/mixed docs still use the DantSu path (unchanged). D32 end-drain stays for the DantSu path.

decisions.decision: Fixed truncated/'stuck' NETWORK prints by adding a post-write DRAIN before closing the socket (the RN foodhub-printer-package's 'smooth network print' technique from its forked DeviceConnection.send: sleep proportional to payload, ~1ms/64 bytes, before close). Our EscPosNetworkPrinter previously closed the socket immediately after DantSu printFormattedText -> large receipts/IMAGE could truncate.
decisions.change: EscPosNetworkPrinter.writeWithTimeout success path: after write, watchdog.cancel() then delay(drainMs(text)) BEFORE disconnectPrinter(). drainMs = (text.length/64).coerceIn(minWriteDrainMs=60, maxWriteDrainMs=2500) (new ctor params). Drain runs AFTER the write-watchdog is cancelled (so the 3s watchdog can't abort the drain); still bounded by the 30s job timeout. Only on successful write (timeout/error paths unchanged).
decisions.analysis_source: Read RN package escpos/escposprinter/connection/DeviceConnection.java + tcp/TcpConnection.java. So Epson/Seiko/Rongta are identical standard DLE EOT => one parser.

decisions.decision: Callback + exception-style print APIs layered over the suspend print()->PrintResult core. Warnings (messages) delivered on a SEPARATE callback from success/error.
decisions.design: New PrintCallback { onWarning(PrinterWarning) {}; onSuccess() {}; onError(PrintResult.Error) {} } (all no-op defaults). Extension fun Printer.print(document, scope, callback): Job launches in the caller's scope and dispatches warnings-first-then-success, or onError (callbacks run on the caller's scope/dispatcher). Exception style: class PrintException(reason, message, cause) + suspend fun Printer.printOrThrow(document): List<PrinterWarning> (returns warnings on success, throws PrintException on error). Both are additive extensions — the sealed PrintResult core is unchanged.

decisions.decision: Two internal SDK robustness improvements to :universal-printer: (1) typed error taxonomy, (2) universal per-job timeout.
decisions.typed_errors: PrintResult.Error gained a 3rd field reason: PrintErrorReason (TIMEOUT, NOT_CONNECTED, PAPER_OUT, COVER_OPEN, PERMISSION_DENIED, CONTENT_INVALID, UNSUPPORTED, IO, UNKNOWN), defaulted last so existing positional Error(msg)/Error(msg,cause) call sites stay source-compatible. Backends now emit reasons: Sunmi surfaces its ALREADY-computed signals (updatePrinterState()==4 -> PAPER_OUT; service unavailable -> NOT_CONNECTED); network + USB via shared escpos/EscPosErrors.escPosReason (EscPosConnectionException/IOException -> NOT_CONNECTED; EscPosParser/Encoding/Barcode -> CONTENT_INVALID); network write-watchdog -> TIMEOUT; USB permission -> PERMISSION_DENIED. Star/iMin left UNKNOWN default for now.
decisions.job_timeout: PrintQueue gained jobTimeoutMs: Long? (null=disabled). Each job runs as an async child; withTimeoutOrNull(jobTimeoutMs){work.await()} else cancel+return Error(reason=TIMEOUT) so the queue ADVANCES past a wedged backend. worker wrapped in runCatching inside async so it can't cancel the worker loop. QueuedPrinter passes DEFAULT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS=30000L (all backends inherit). CAVEAT: a blocking (non-suspending) vendor call is only truly abandoned when a spare dispatcher thread exists — true on default Dispatchers.IO, not on a single-thread dispatcher (documented on PrintQueue).

decisions.decision: EscPosNetworkPrinter timeouts: connectTimeoutMs default 4000 (was 5000), new writeTimeoutMs default 3000.
decisions.connect_timeout_VERIFIED: javap -c of DantSu TcpConnection.connect() shows Socket.connect(InetSocketAddress, int) using the ctor's timeout int => that param IS the connect timeout. Set to 4000.
decisions.write_timeout_rationale: DantSu print path is WRITE-ONLY (DeviceConnection.send -> outputStream.write+flush, no read; verified from bytecode — no setSoTimeout call, socket field private w/ no getter). Java SO_TIMEOUT bounds blocking READS only, so it cannot cap a print write. Implemented a 3s cap via a watchdog coroutine (launch{ delay(writeTimeoutMs); connection.disconnect() }) that force-closes the socket at the deadline — the only thing that unblocks a wedged TCP write; the resulting write exception is mapped to PrintResult.Error('...timed out after 3000ms'). timedOut tracked via AtomicBoolean (cross-thread visibility). Requires a multi-threaded dispatcher (default Dispatchers.IO) so the watchdog runs while the write blocks; documented on the class.

decisions.decision: Retry mechanism for connectivity failures on the network (TCP/9100 ESC/POS) printer. Wired into EscPosNetworkPrinter.doConnect + doPrint; UniversalPrinter.network(host,port,retryPolicy=DEFAULT) exposes it.
decisions.safety_design: Retry wraps ONLY the connect/handshake phase, NOT the write. VERIFIED by javap: EscPosPrinter(connection,...) CONSTRUCTOR throws EscPosConnectionException (DantSu connects at construction, before any byte on the wire) => re-opening the socket cannot double-print. printFormattedText*(text) (the write) is a single attempt because raw 9100 has no app-level ack, so a mid-stream reset may have already printed part of the receipt and replay would duplicate. Each retry attempt disconnects the prior TcpConnection + builds a fresh one.
decisions.retryable_predicate_VERIFIED: isConnectivityError = EscPosConnectionException || java.io.IOException. javap-confirmed EscPosConnectionException extends java.lang.Exception (NOT IOException), thrown by TcpConnection.connect() and EscPosPrinter ctor/printFormattedText. Content errors (EscPosParser/Encoding/Barcode) are deterministic => NOT retried. USB printer intentionally out of scope (attach/permission issue, not transient).

decisions.decision: SOLID/structure hardening of the discovery tier: introduced the missing abstraction layer. (1) fun interface PrinterDiscoverer { suspend fun discover(): List<DiscoveredPrinter> } — facade discoverAll() now folds over a List<PrinterDiscoverer> + a new additionalDiscoverers ctor param, so adding a mechanism = register one more, no facade edit (fixes OCP). (2) interface SnmpTransport implemented by SnmpClient; SnmpIdentityProbe depends on SnmpTransport not the concrete client (fixes DIP + makes probe() unit-testable with a fake). (3) Injected CoroutineDispatcher (default Dispatchers.IO) into SnmpClient/SnmpDiscovery/ZebraDiscovery/EpsonDiscovery per android-dev skill guidance.
decisions.rationale: Code review with android-skills:android-dev found SRP/packaging production-grade but OCP weak (facade hardcoded the flow list) and DIP partial (constructor injection onto concrete FINAL classes — proven by tests only being able to cover pure functions, not probe()). The interface layer lifts OCP+DIP to green and unlocks full testability.
decisions.verified: BUILD SUCCESSFUL (lib + example assembleDebug); testDebugUnitTest tests=16 failures=0 (SnmpIdentityProbeTest 5->8: added probe() tests via a FakeSnmpTransport — the DIP payoff). Behavior preserved: discoverAll still branded-first (Epson ENPC first) via registration order + distinctBy(ip).
decisions.not_done: Dispatcher injection NOT propagated to the lower probes/transports (EpsonTcpProbe, EpsonUdpDiscovery, EscPosSerialProbe, NetworkScanner) — only the top-level orchestrators + SnmpClient. Concrete discoverers still don't implement PrinterDiscoverer directly (facade wraps them as SAM adapters, context bound per-call). Both acceptable; revisit if deeper dispatcher-swap tests are needed.

decisions.decision: Added Star Micronics, Zebra, Bixolon, Citizen, Brother discovery SDK-free. GENERALIZED the Seiko SNMP flow (D7) into a brand-agnostic SNMP flow (network/seiko -> network/snmp) + added a Zebra UDP-4201 flow (network/zebra). PARTIALLY SUPERSEDES D1's Star/Zebra exclusion for DISCOVERY only (printing still needs each vendor SDK).
decisions.rationale: User directive (showed the 5-brand research table): 'we have to add these brands.' Research (2026-07-16): 4 of 5 (Star/Bixolon/Citizen/Brother) identify over standard SNMP/Printer-MIB — same mechanism as Seiko — so one brand-agnostic SNMP flow with a sysDescr token->brand map covers them all + folds Seiko in. Zebra needs its own protocol: documented SDK-free UDP-4201 broadcast (request 2E2C3A010000; reply 3A2C2E..03 with model@0x0C/serial@0x38/hostname@0x54, no MAC -> MAC via SNMP). Mirrors EpsonUdpDiscovery.
decisions.user_choices: GROUPED API: discoverSnmpPrinters() (all SNMP brands + GENERIC-with-identity in one sweep) + discoverZebraPrinters(); caller reads DiscoveredPrinter.brand. ENRICHED generic scan: discoverNetworkPrinters() now SNMP-enriches each hit (IP+MAC+model+serial; GENERIC IP-only if no SNMP).

decisions.decision: Seiko RP-series receipt printers (RP-E10/E11, RP-D10, RP-F10) are now IN scope, added SDK-free via SNMP. PARTIALLY SUPERSEDES the RP portion of D1's Seiko exclusion and the 'no SDK-free path' conclusion in D6.seiko. Does NOT change the SLP720/721RT label printers — those remain OUT (still need the Sii SDK / a device capture).
decisions.rationale: User directive: 'implement seiko printer search without sdk'. Research (2026-07-16) confirmed RP-series are Ethernet + industry-standard ESC/POS and, like ~all networked POS printers, expose SNMP/MIB on UDP/161 — the vendor-neutral, SDK-free way to read make/model/serial. Discovery reuses the existing TCP-9100 /24 sweep (NetworkScanner) to find live hosts, then a hand-rolled SNMPv1 GET (raw DatagramSocket, no snmp4j) reads standard OIDs to positively identify Seiko. No proprietary jar; AAR stays clean.
decisions.implementation: network/seiko/Snmp.kt (BER codec) + SnmpClient.kt (UDP/161 GET) + SeikoSnmpProbe.kt (OID orchestration + brand match) + SeikoDiscovery.kt (sweep -> SNMP identify). Facade: discoverSeikoPrinters(), probeSeiko(ip), discoverAll() merge, PrinterBrand.SEIKO. Example: Seiko button. Unit test SnmpTest (5 cases, all pass).

SEIKO_TOKENS, OIDs, and community are all overridable so a real-device capture can tune them without structural change. NOT run against real RP hardware.

findings.epson: VERIFIED: MAC via ENPC UDP (offset 54) + serial via GS I 68 (1D 49 44) TCP-9100. Implemented (EpsonUdpDiscovery + EpsonTcpProbe).
findings.sunmi: VERIFIED: serial via GS I 68 (foodhub customQuerySn() == GS_I_SERIAL == 1D 49 44); MAC via ARP (<=Android9). IMPLEMENTED this session: new EscPosSerialProbe (brand-agnostic GS I 68) wired into SunmiDiscovery.enrichIdentity + best-effort ARP MAC.
findings.rongta: PARTIAL: Rongta RP325/326/327/328 command set does NOT support GS I (verified via ManualsLib RP325 command set). It exposes serial/firmware/manufacturer/name via GS ( H (1D 28 48 ...) per that manual (p37), BUT the exact request params (pL pH fn m) + response layout could NOT be extracted (Chinese/binary PDFs, 403s). Discovery: generic TCP-9100 scan works (default IP 192.168.1.87, port 9100); Rongta setup tool uses a UDP broadcast whose exact port/packet is in an un-extractable PDF. DECISION: do NOT ship guessed GS ( H bytes; Rongta is discoverable via the generic scan, serial/MAC deferred until a real-device packet capture or the exact p37 spec is obtained.
findings.seiko: NOT VERIFIED SDK-free: Seiko SLP720/721RT is ESC/POS-compatible over TCP-9100 but no public command for programmatic serial/MAC was found; the original app used the proprietary Sii SDK (SiiAndroidSDK.jar). Hardware serial only via a front-panel button combo. DECISION: Seiko identity stays OUT of the SDK-free core (needs the Sii SDK or a device capture).

decisions.decision: Sunmi cloud-printer discovery ADDED to the SDK, SDK-free — PARTIALLY SUPERSEDES D1's exclusion of Sunmi. Implemented via Android NsdManager (DNS-SD/mDNS), not the Sunmi jar.
decisions.rationale: Verified by decompiling com.sunmi:external-printerlibrary2:1.0.13 (downloaded from Maven Central; javap on classes.jar): its LanHelper does LAN discovery via NsdManager.discoverServices with service type '_afpovertcp._tcp.', resolves each service, and filters to service names starting with 'CloudPrint_' (CloudPrinterBuilder). No proprietary protocol — NsdManager is a platform API — so it is reimplementable SDK-free, exactly like the Epson ENPC port. The UDP-17899 multicast some Sunmi docs mention is NOT used by 1.0.13 (grepped the jar: no 17899/MulticastSocket).
decisions.evidence: network/sunmi/SunmiDiscovery.kt; SERVICE_TYPE='_afpovertcp._tcp.', name prefix 'CloudPrint_', ip=resolved host, port=resolved port.
decisions.caveat: resolveService is deprecated in API 34 (use registerServiceInfoCallback on 34+ as a follow-up). MAC/serial not available via this mDNS path; brand tagged SUNMI, name = mDNS service name. Runtime verification against a real Sunmi cloud printer NOT done.

decisions.decision: Scope the SDK to the THREE SDK-free discovery flows only: Epson network (ENPC/UDP + GS I TCP probe), generic IP (TCP-9100 subnet sweep), and USB (UsbManager). EXCLUDE Star/Sunmi/Seiko/Zebra.
decisions.rationale: Star (stario10), Sunmi (external-printerlibrary2), Seiko/Sii (SiiAndroidSDK.jar), and Zebra (ZSDK_ANDROID_API.jar) each require a proprietary SDK/jar that cannot be redistributed in an open library. The three chosen flows use only raw sockets + platform APIs, so the AAR is clean to publish.
